cases.exposure_context_quote: the child was playing unsupervised in a storage area near the farm, after which he developed vomiting, drowsiness, and abdominal bloating. There was no witnessed ingestion, but a strong chemical odor was noted on his clothes, and a dichlorvos container was discovered in the vicinity.
cases.agent: organophosphate pesticide, dichlorvos (suspected; container found nearby; no laboratory confirmation)
cases.agent_quote: approximately five hours after suspected exposure to an OP pesticide, dichlorvos
cases.circumstance: unintentional exposure while playing unsupervised in a storage area near the farm in a rural farming community with frequent domestic pesticide use

symptoms.finding: altered level of consciousness (GCS 8/15), vomiting, abdominal distension
symptoms.quote: A 5-year-old, 11-month-old male presented with an altered level of consciousness and progressive abdominal distension approximately five hours after suspected exposure to an OP pesticide, dichlorvos.

symptoms.finding: pinpoint pupils, sluggish reflexes, tachypnea (RR 40), SpO2 72% room air, bilateral crepitations
symptoms.quote: On arrival, the child was drowsy (Glasgow Coma Scale 8/15), with pinpoint pupils, sluggish reflexes, and a strong pesticide smell. He was tachypneic (respiratory rate 40/minute), with an oxygen saturation of 72% on room air

symptoms.finding: paralytic ileus: globally distended, rigid, tympanic abdomen, silent for five minutes; dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels on X-ray
symptoms.quote: An erect abdominal X-ray revealed dilated bowel loops and multiple air-fluid levels suggestive of intestinal obstruction

symptoms.finding: aspiration pneumonitis (bilateral haziness on chest X-ray)
symptoms.quote: Chest X-ray showed bilateral haziness, indicating possible aspiration pneumonitis (Figure 1B).

cases.time_to_care: approximately five hours after suspected exposure

labs.name: laboratory examinations
labs.value: presented in Table 1 (values not included in source text); serum cholinesterase unavailable
labs.quote: Confirmatory testing, including serum cholinesterase levels, was unavailable.

treatment.name: oxygen therapy and gastric lavage
treatment.quote: Initial management included oxygen therapy and gastric lavage.

treatment.name: atropine IV 0.8 mg every 5-10 minutes
treatment.quote: Atropine was administered intravenously (0.8 mg every 5-10 minutes) with close monitoring.

treatment.name: pralidoxime 50 mg/kg IV repeatedly after one hour
treatment.quote: Pralidoxime (50 mg/kg intravenous) was given repeatedly after one hour.

treatment.name: supportive: IV fluids, dexamethasone, mannitol, broad-spectrum antibiotics, analgesics, nasogastric decompression, suctioning
treatment.quote: Supportive measures included intravenous fluids, dexamethasone, mannitol, broad-spectrum antibiotics, analgesics, and nasogastric decompression.

cases.outcome: survived; full recovery by day 5, discharged tolerating feeds with no neurological deficits
cases.outcome_quote: There was full recovery by day 5, and he was discharged, tolerating feeds and with no neurological deficits. Post-discharge follow-up at two weeks confirmed complete recovery
cases.sequelae: none reported (complete recovery confirmed at two-week follow-up)
cases.notes: Diagnosis made clinically without laboratory confirmation; surgical consultation excluded mechanical obstruction.
